overall:
Verdict: the eight reports find real faults, and I confirmed the important ones in the code, but added together they are over-built for one owner with four Sparks. They propose about 80 gaps and 28 new action names on top of today's 36. Seven of those names are three designs of one container runner (save/run/stop_workload, run_box/stop_box, run_job/job_result), four are one on/off switch (self_healing, change_setting, settings, pause_changes), and two are one call (restart_sparkie, start_sparkie). There are four ways to save what just ran, three page readers, five new state files and several new verb lists for the gate. The service is already 9,250 long lines (574 KB built) that Sparkie is meant to maintain alone, and all 36 actions are Sparkie's tools today (service/src/14-chats.mjs:60).

My cut keeps roughly a third and builds each shared idea once: seven new actions (start_sparkie, pause_changes, download_model, run_workload, stop_workload, read_page, update_console), one new state file (workload specs), no new background loop, and test_changes removed.

Order.
1. Make what is installed true (all small): the carry-on race, the installer's stale-lock hole, heals that can stop a newer model, run_workflow running a name nobody said, a stopped brain that stays down, the owner's API being weaker than the page, and a re-start that deletes the working container before the new one is proven.
2. Give the six page-only paths an action, then delete: most of the 5,292-line page, members and sharing, the short address and door socket, the workers.dev push, the editor and file browser, chat routing, about 40 REST copies, hand-started recipe approval, three brain presets and the YaRN overlay, the `local` installer mode, Spark 1 from config.json while it is locked out, and the contract down to what is built. Also the 'validated on these Sparks' second gate: the owner's own request, a saved workflow, an API call and self-healing already count as the validation run (16-actions.mjs:330, 20-heal.mjs:81), so it now only adds a question for outside agents, while nearly every report lists 'needs a validation run' as a risk. Keep the 'tested' lock. This deletion needs the owner's yes because tests pin it.
3. Repeat: context and parallel on start_model, the usual setup, heal and undo carrying the setup, 'save that as X' built from the audit record, pair verbs, remembering what an off Spark holds, download_model, open problems, one heal decider, a multi-message eval.
4. Independent: git on Spark 2, the gate in a container, a small update_console with a four-line probe, the watchdog's one-time put-back.
5. Anything: one workload runner (services on Spark 2 first, then jobs) and one page reader.
Waits for a real request: GPU services, a port per model, plugs and power, schedules, change_console, try_fix and learned-fix records, file and service pass-through routes, delete_model and free_disk, brain tuning.

State of the tree: the brief is out of date. docs/reviews-2026-11-11.md lines 85-91 record build c0789b85fa67 (memory, carry-on, POST /actions, watchdog, source on Spark 2) as installed and checked live today, so the carry-on race is live on Spark 2. While I read, the tree moved again: its build is 4f371d567af6 and service/workflows.lock.json still says c0789b85fa67, so an install now would switch every workflow off without a warning. Start the build from GET /health, not from the brief. I ran nothing, changed nothing and called nothing live; upstream claims (the SGLang issue, GB10 memory limits) I did not re-check.

rulings.proposal: Gap 1: save_workload, run_workload, stop_workload with a spec store (19-workloads.mjs)
rulings.why: This is the right runner and the only one that should be built: learning's run_box and stop_box, chatapi's run_job and job_result and combine's 'tool template' are the same thing designed three more times. As written it still carries more than a first version needs: a separate save action, a gpu flag, written files, a `set` input and a budget table.
rulings.instead: One part, two actions: run_workload {name} or {name, spec}, and stop_workload {name}. A new spec asks the owner once; when its check passes, code keeps it under its name (as recordVerified does for model starts), so there is no save action and no copy in saved-workflows.json. First version: services only, CPU-only, on Spark 2 under a memory cap, network off unless the first-run question shows it. Fields: name, image, command, env, port, check, memoryGB, net. Label spark.workload, never spark.console (the draft at /private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-akuppala-Documents-26aiRAG/aeda3f21-5bf5-4ab2-97c9-eb9169fa6d77/scratchpad/19-apps.mjs line 46 sets spark.console=1 and spark.model). No new verb list: run needs the name in the owner's words. If the owner says no to Spark 2, do not build services at all, because GLM fills Spark 3 and 4.

rulings.proposal: Gap 2: watchServices (restart a service that fails its check for 10 minutes; bring services back on Spark 3 or 4)
rulings.why: The first version has no services on Spark 3 or 4, and the healing report itself skipped hang watches for models because no hang has been seen. A fourth heal path for a search box is not worth it.
rulings.instead: Start services with Docker's --restart unless-stopped, as the brain is (13-main-model.mjs:128). A service that is down or failing its check is one line in open problems. Add a restart rule the first time a real hang is seen.

rulings.proposal: Gap 3: job kind (scripts Sparkie writes and runs)
rulings.why: Needed for 'do anything', but it is the part most likely to fail on a 27B model (a script quoted inside JSON), and it adds result plumbing: exit watching, a result notice, time limits and carry-on rules. Nothing yet shows the brain can write a working spec.
rulings.instead: Build after services have run for real and after a schema-only eval (ten 'set up X' and 'run this' prompts graded against the spec schema; no runner needed). Then: CPU jobs on Spark 2 only, network off by default, Docker as the record (a label carries the chat id), and the watcher posts the exit code and last 40 lines. Leave GPU jobs, jobs as workflow steps and file hand-over for later.

rulings.proposal: Gap 4, part 2: find_recipes returns catalog.json playbooks as guides with image and ports
rulings.why: I opened service/catalog.json: its 29 playbooks hold only id, title, description, category, sparks and url. There is no image, port or step to return, and Sparkie has no tool that can read the url.
rulings.instead: Return the 29 as title and link (a few lines) and pair them with the one page reader (see the ruling on independence gap 8). Without a reader a guide is a dead link.

rulings.proposal: Gap 4, part 4 (also brain gap 6): save every finished multi-step request by itself, as a workflow or a draft
rulings.why: Four reports answer this four ways (auto-save 20, drafts of 10 that expire, a button, only on request). Auto-saved names land in Sparkie's prompt and are named from a sentence the owner will never say again. The owner's 'I will forget to ask' rule is already met where the thinking was expensive: a model start keeps its setup and a workload keeps its spec on its first passing run.
rulings.instead: The done line of a multi-step request ends with: Say 'save that as <name>' to keep it. No drafts, no cap, no expiry.

rulings.proposal: Gap 7: GPU services (ComfyUI, speech) with declared memory
rulings.why: Declared memory is a promise, not a cap. A runaway image or video job freezes a Spark until someone power-cycles it, Spark 4 is on Wi-Fi only, and GLM fills both GPU Sparks most days. It also changes plan() and memoryShare, the heart of every start.
rulings.instead: Wait until the owner names a GPU app. Then allow one per Spark, only on a Spark that holds no model at that moment.

rulings.proposal: Gap 8: a host port per model
rulings.why: It touches 19 uses of the port across 7 files and all three start paths, and beside GLM across Spark 3 and 4 there is no memory left to use it. The backlog already says later.
rulings.instead: Keep one model per Spark. Revisit when the two Sparks routinely run separate small models.

rulings.proposal: Gaps 9 and 10: a file PUT/GET route and a /svc pass-through
rulings.why: Two new unparsed streams on an address that is open to the internet, for needs nobody has yet. The report itself says build on first use.
rulings.instead: Nothing until an agent first needs to send a file or call a service from off the tailnet.

rulings.proposal: Gap 1 (also chatapi 2d, combine 4, brain 3 and 6): saved names in Sparkie's prompt, and run_workflow clear only when its title is in the owner's words
rulings.why: Five reports propose it; build it once. Today any message with a start verb clears any saved workflow: ACTION_KIND maps run_workflow to 'start' (16-actions.mjs:159) and tracesToRequest checks only model, container and Spark inputs, which run_workflow does not have.
rulings.instead: First batch, in this order: the title gate, then the names in the prompt (at most 12 lines). Never put names in the prompt before the gate is in.

rulings.proposal: Gap 2 and gap 9: run_box, stop_box and serve mode, cleared whenever the owner's message is an instruction
rulings.why: As written, Sparkie chooses the script, the image and whether the network is on, and it runs with no question whenever the message is an instruction. A script shaped by a web page or a log, with the network on, can reach the home network from inside the container. It is also the second design of the same runner, and its 'kill below 4 GB free' rule is the console-side memory valve the healing report rejected.
rulings.instead: Drop run_box, stop_box and serve mode; use the one workload runner. The first run of any new spec asks the owner once and shows the image, the network setting and the script. Saved specs then run by name with no question.

rulings.proposal: Gap 3: passing runs saved as one-step workflows, with defaults, a cap of 40 and expiring drafts
rulings.why: It makes two registries for one thing (the spec and a workflow that wraps it) and adds cap, expiry and 'version it replaces' bookkeeping.
rulings.instead: The spec store is the registry and `workloads` lists it; a saved workflow may still call run_workload as a step. Keep one small piece: job.result on an operation (last output, files, address) so wait_operation returns it. Fix fillIn so a script's braces are left alone when the job kind arrives.

rulings.proposal: Gap 4: a try loop with 6 tries per name per day and its own minutes limit
rulings.why: New counters beside the three budgets that already exist.
rulings.instead: Set the chat's task after any run Sparkie started and let the existing carry-on budget bound it (8 turns, 2 hours, 12 changes for the whole request). The failed notice carries the last 2,000 characters of output, marked as data.

rulings.proposal: Gap 5: stale flags from input hashes, a 'failing' state after two runs, 'use the old way', a 15-minute wait on a step's question
rulings.why: State machines for a handful of saved routines. The real brittleness is two things: a saved stop names a container that has gone (stop_model answers 404), and step arguments are checked only when they run.
rulings.instead: Three small changes: check every step with checkInput at save and before step 1; stop_model with only a Spark stops everything Spark Console runs there, and a stop that is already true counts as done; record who really saved it. Whether a saved workflow may stop an in-use model without asking is one owner decision. Drop the hashes, the failing state, the version swap and the waiting run.

rulings.proposal: Gap 6 (also chatapi 2c, brain 6, combine 4): four ways to save what just ran: fromChat, operations:[ids], from:'last', fromRunning
rulings.why: Four designs, and two add a store. The exact record is already on disk: every runAction writes the action, masked arguments, chat id, outcome and operation id to audit.jsonl (20-mcp.mjs:124-128, written at 16-actions.mjs:369).
rulings.instead: One input: save_workflow {title, from: 'last'}. Code reads this chat's completed changes for the last request from the audit lines, in order; Sparkie supplies only the title. Widen the save pattern to 'save or keep that as <name>'. No ops.jsonl, no arguments copied into chats.json, no fromRunning, no button.

rulings.proposal: Gap 7 (also brain gap 8): the eval, listed after the features it should judge
rulings.why: Both reports place it late, yet it decides whether the later gaps are worth building. The carry-on race passed the suite only because the stand-in model answers instantly.
rulings.instead: Second batch: cases of several messages graded from the audit, about 25 cases (not 50 run three times), run by test/eval.mjs when the prompt, tools or setup change. No score_sparkie action, no sparkie_stats and no eval-candidates file until someone has read a first report.

rulings.proposal: Gap 8: find_playbook, an index and reader for NVIDIA's playbooks
rulings.why: One of three proposed readers (find_playbook, read_page, guides). A second index of one repository and a tool for one source.
rulings.instead: One reader, read_page, which also reads a playbook's README when the owner or a guide names its address.

rulings.proposal: Gap 10 (and chatapi gap 9): schedules on saved workflows, and their rails
rulings.why: The owner did not ask for timed runs and wants no notifications, and bring-back at power-on already covers the common trigger. A 60-second scheduler with pause rules is a new loop that acts with nobody watching.
rulings.instead: Nothing now. If asked later: three fixed forms, proven routines only, healing's counters, never a download and never an answer to a question.

rulings.proposal: Gap 4: update_console with updater.sh, probe.sh, path classification, update.json and a 30-minute watchdog probe
rulings.why: The action is what removes the Mac, so it stays. Classifying changed paths with a passkey question only matters once Sparkie writes code, which is deferred. The 30-minute watchdog probe duplicates healing gap 5's one-time put-back.
rulings.instead: update_console {testOnly?}: the owner's words in chat or the owner's own POST /actions, never an agent key. It runs gate.sh, waits until idle, runs install.sh through systemd-run (as undo_update does, 18-workflows.mjs:383), then a four-line probe: health shows the new build, whoami says owner, a keyless internet request gets 401, one chat turn ends. The installer puts the old build back on failure. The result is posted in the chat at the next start. No path lists yet. First drill: a comment-only change.

rulings.proposal: Gap 8: update_console with a patch input
rulings.why: A patch sent over the API is code that runs as the console's user on the hub. The independence report rejects the same idea, and this report's own text says a protected-file list does not make it safe.
rulings.instead: Code reaches Spark 2 through git over the owner's SSH. update_console only tests and installs what is in the checkout.

rulings.proposal: Gap 5: the engine trial, then change_console
rulings.why: The only run on record is a dry run with 0 passes, so whether a 27B can fix this code is unknown, and nothing can use the answer until update_console works.
rulings.instead: Run the trial once (Qwen Code first) after update_console has passed its drills. Build change_console only at 2 of 3. If the answer is 'not yet', remove the second engine from agentbar and keep only the image the gate uses.

rulings.proposal: Gap 6: internetUp() with a 'down since' tracker in fleet_status and a saved recipe index
rulings.why: A new probe and cached state for a rare case. The valuable half is moving image pulls and weight copies ahead of the stops, which configs gap 2 also needs.
rulings.instead: Build pull-and-copy-before-stop once, with configs gap 2. Fix the untrue messages where the fetch fails: search_huggingface returns an error instead of no results, and a repo start says Hugging Face could not be reached. Skip the tracker and the saved index.

rulings.proposal: Gap 8: seed memory, apply the staged work, console_docs and read_page
rulings.why: Steps 1 and 2 are done: docs/reviews-2026-11-11.md lines 85-91 record memory seeded with twelve lines and the API batch installed. console_docs would hand Sparkie a 1,411-line contract that mostly describes things not built and says the code is wrong where they differ. read_page as written fetches any https address from the hub; with redirects it can reach the home network, tailnet addresses and the brain's own port.
rulings.instead: One reader only: read_page {url}. The address must be in the owner's words or come from a guide; https only; refuse private, loopback, link-local and 100.64/10 addresses, also after a redirect; cap the size; mark the text as outside text. Defer console_docs until the contract is cut to what is built.

rulings.proposal: Gap 10: a --socket transport in tools/spark.mjs and tools/console.mjs
rulings.why: The owner can already do this with one curl line on the socket, as the watchdog does. The report rates it low itself.
rulings.instead: Write the curl line in the recovery page. If console.mjs gains `ask` and `do <action>`, delete tools/spark.mjs so there is one command-line tool.

rulings.proposal: Gap 3: forget_should_run and self_healing actions
rulings.why: Three reports add an action for the same switch (self_healing, change_setting, pause_changes) and two add a separate 'forget' verb. The openProblems function itself is worth keeping.
rulings.instead: Keep openProblems: five lines first in Sparkie's notes, the full list in fleet_status, a count in /health. stop_model on a listed entry that is not running takes it off the list (combine gap 1c). One switch action, pause_changes {on}; ask the owner to drop the separate self-heal switch.

rulings.proposal: Gap 6: try_fix with a closed fix list
rulings.why: Once start_model takes context and parallel, 'start it again with one thing changed' is start_model. A second start path with its own list, budget and gate words duplicates it, and each wrong guess on GLM costs a 12-minute load.
rulings.instead: After a failed start in the owner's chat, Sparkie gets one turn to read the log and say the cause. A retry with a changed setting comes back as one button ('Start X with a 32k context?'), because the number is not in the owner's words. A retry that works is kept as that model's setup, so the next chat or API start reuses it.

rulings.proposal: Gap 7: problems.json of learned fixes matched by cause line, with forget_fix
rulings.why: It carries a lesson from one model to another. One owner runs a handful of models, the same new failure on a second model is rare, and verified.json already reuses a fix for the same model. It is a new store, a new action and a silent change to what a start does.
rulings.instead: Keep the small half now: mark a setup that failed in verified.json so bestHow tries it last for 7 days. Revisit learned fixes after the same cause has been fixed by hand twice.

rulings.proposal: Gap 8 (also independence gap 7): watch key expiry, certificate, disk, backup age, linger, cable changes and a daily Hugging Face sign-in check
rulings.why: Two reports propose it; build once. The cable event and the daily Hugging Face check are extra: the second sends a token out every day to learn what the 'gated' failure already says when it matters.
rulings.instead: Four lines in open problems, each from a call the console already makes: a Tailscale key within 21 days of expiry, linger off, free disk low, no backup for 2 days. Retry the backup when a Spark comes online.

rulings.proposal: Gap 9: settle interrupted operations at start-up (adopt, or stop leftovers and start again what was stopped)
rulings.why: An automatic stop-and-restart pass at every console start is a new way for things to stop with nobody asking. Updates will wait until idle, so a cut-off operation stays rare.
rulings.instead: At start-up, a model that a cut-off start left running and answering is added to the should-run list and its chat is told. Anything else is one line in open problems. No automatic stops.

rulings.proposal: Gap 10: download and pull retries, a longer wait for a silent Spark, log size caps and free_disk
rulings.why: The retries are worth it on a 178 GB download over Wi-Fi. free_disk is a deleting action, and chatapi adds a second one (delete_model); AGENTS.md says never delete the owner's data.
rulings.instead: Keep the stalled-download retry (3 tries), the log size cap on new containers and the longer wait during a pair load. Defer free_disk and delete_model together; until then a low-disk line in open problems names the folder and its size.

rulings.proposal: Gap 2: ops.jsonl, arguments stored in chats, a 'Save these steps' button, carry-on for ask_sparkie conversations
rulings.why: audit.jsonl already holds each call with its arguments, chat and operation id. A button cannot take a name and an API caller cannot press it. Carrying on for agents adds brain turns before carry-on is proven in the owner's own chat.
rulings.instead: recent_operations joins the audit record, so each operation shows its action and arguments, also after a restart. Saving is the one sentence 'save that as X' (the from:'last' input). Leave ask_sparkie conversations as they are for now.

rulings.proposal: Gap 6: a why_failed action
rulings.why: A 37th read tool that joins facts the failed operation already has: startWithFixes puts the known problem, its advice and the cause lines into the job's error (17-changes.mjs:285-293), and wait_operation returns the error, what was fixed and the last log lines.
rulings.instead: Add three fields to what a failed operation already returns (wait_operation, operation_log and the chat notice): cause, tried, next. Stop pointing at 'Activity' (14-chats.mjs:122).

rulings.proposal: Gap 7: run_job and job_result (19-jobs.mjs)
rulings.why: The third design of the same container runner, on Spark 3 or 4 only, where GLM usually leaves no room.
rulings.instead: The one workload runner; its job kind covers this.

rulings.proposal: Gap 10: remove the page's copies last (rated L, medium), and add delete_model
rulings.why: The owner asked to prefer removing. Every later batch has to keep the page routes and their tests green and wait for a longer gate. It is listed tenth.
rulings.instead: Second batch, right after the six page-only paths have an action (pause_changes, start_sparkie, stop_model on a held entry, find_setups adding a repo, linked_sparks {test:true}, download_model). Delete: members, invites and access requests; the short address and door socket; the workers.dev push and /public routes (cloud/, deploy/web-page.sh, deploy/short-address.sh, pushCloud in 23-http.mjs); the editor proxy and file browser; chat routing (ROUTES, /main/route); the REST copies; the page down to chat, sign-in, keys and a status strip; hand-started recipe approval (19-watcher.mjs:120-136); the 'validated' gate with test_changes and validateChanged. Port the tests to /actions; never drop them. Defer delete_model.

rulings.proposal: Gap 1 (also usecases gap 6 and chatapi gap 3): new start_model inputs: context, atOnce, memoryPercent, engine, image, flags, once, quant, category
rulings.why: Three reports give three schemas with different names. Each optional input is one more place for a 27B to put a number. The owner's sentence is 'a 64k context, 8 at once'; engine and image already travel in a setup id.
rulings.instead: Two typed inputs, context and parallel, each required to be in the owner's words; `setup` also accepts a past run's id or 'best'. New settings on a running model restart it where it is. Add flags, image, a memory share or category only when a real request needs one. Ship in the same batch as configs gap 2, never before it.

rulings.proposal: Gaps 4 and 6: settings and change_setting with nine keys
rulings.why: A settings system for one owner. The default home is a bug, not a setting (pickVersion never reads modelsHost, 17-changes.mjs:354). Protected names change a few times a year. Sparkie's thinking and limits are picked once by the eval. The hourly limit stops mattering once the owner's own requests no longer count toward it.
rulings.instead: One action, pause_changes {on}: the owner's own POST /actions can resume while paused, and chat shows one button. fleet_status shows the pause, the build and the last backup. Fix pickVersion to prefer the default home when the model fits there.

rulings.proposal: Gap 7: preset hash label, restartPending, a test prompt before a switch is kept
rulings.why: The owner switches the brain a few times a year from a terminal and knows when they did.
rulings.instead: Keep two things. Delete aphex, aphex-x4, aphex-agent and the YaRN overlay, with the owner's yes because tests pin them. Make loadMainSetup refuse to fall back silently: today a missing saved id falls to the first preset, which is aphex with thinking off (13-main-model.mjs:12-16; config.json lists aphex first).

rulings.proposal: Gap 8: keep the previous copy of a replaced workflow, with restore
rulings.why: One more input and state for a mistake the reply already reports ('replaced'), with the state folder copied daily.
rulings.instead: Keep only the argument check at save.

rulings.proposal: Gap 3e and gap 4: 'move' and 'migrate' verbs, fromRunning, grouped undo
rulings.why: Each verb is another regular expression in the gate with its own false matches ('move on'). fromRunning is the fourth save design. Undoing a whole run means several 12-minute loads chosen by code.
rulings.instead: Keep 3a to 3d: a start on the same Sparks answers 'already', a named start stops a pair as a pair, restart_model works on a pair, stop everything on a Spark. To go back after a mode switch the owner says the other mode's name.

rulings.proposal: Gap 5: self-healing stops the leftover half of a pair, and restarts a silent pair
rulings.why: Nobody has seen what the Spark 3 half does when Spark 4 goes off (the report says inferred, never observed), and this is the first rule that lets healing stop something. The healing report skipped hang watches for the same reason.
rulings.instead: Report it truthfully now: a pair counts as running only when every part runs, should_be_running says 'held: Spark 4 is off', and the gateway stops listing it. Watch one real power-off, then decide.

rulings.proposal: Gaps 6 and 7: power_spark off now; smart plugs, power-on and a guarded power cycle later
rulings.why: Two other reports list power as not worth it now. Off-only needs a sudo rule the owner adds by hand and a new 'power' verb that collides with 'turn off gemma', and it leaves a Spark nobody can turn back on from chat. The power cycle cuts mains to a machine on two inferred signals.
rulings.instead: Build on and off together, only once two metering plugs are on the LAN and the owner has checked that Spark 4 boots when power returns. Leave the unattended power cycle out of that first version.

rulings.proposal: Gap 8: an embedder and reranker on Spark 2 as a 'tool template' in 19-apps.mjs
rulings.why: The report itself says worth it only when a use case needs it, and it is a fourth container design.
rulings.instead: When a documents use is real, it is one CPU-only spec on the workload runner, and runningModels lists it for the gateway. Do keep usecases gap 5 now (the embeddings done-check): it is small and fixes a misleading failure.

rulings.proposal: Gap 9, part 4: pin NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX for pairs
rulings.why: Two forum posters saw it; it has not been seen here. It changes the pair start, and the plain-sockets retry already recovers the case.
rulings.instead: Keep parts 1 to 3: linked_sparks {test:true}, Spark 2's pairs no longer advertised, and the copy path inside download_model.

rulings.proposal: Gap 2: brainCheck inside switchMain, POST /main/check and a check_sparkie action
rulings.why: The measurement matters and should happen before anything else is built on 4 at once. It does not need an action, a route and a hook in the switch: a switch is already the owner's terminal command, and the cut-stream and one-token probes can crash the live brain.
rulings.instead: tools/brain-check.mjs: the parallel-versus-serial comparison, run once on today's setup at a quiet time and called by tools/brain-setup.mjs after a switch. Write the result in the contract's progress section. Run the crash probes by hand, once.

rulings.proposal: Gap 4 (also independence 2, healing 1, chatapi 5b): bring back a stopped or missing brain
rulings.why: Four reports propose it under two action names. It is the one failure that leaves only SSH, so it belongs in the first batch, built once.
rulings.instead: One action, start_sparkie (saved setup only, hidden from Sparkie's own tools). The watch must run even when the owner has paused changes or switched self-healing off: today healPass returns before watchBrain in both cases (20-heal.mjs:139-140). An owner's own stop is respected. Chat answers 'starting; ask again in a minute' in place of 'Start it from Models' (14-chats.mjs:282).

overall:
The eight areas agree on the lines that matter most, and I checked the code they rest on: no host shell, no Keeper, no action for SSH, Tailscale, the firewall, users or keys, and no tool that switches the brain. Nothing proposed touches SSH or Tailscale directly, so a hard lock-out needs an indirect path. I found those paths in four new powers: code a model wrote running in containers, the console installing its own updates, more things healing or retrying by themselves, and saved workflows becoming stored programs.

The findings that change the plan:
- Saved workflows are a way round every gate. Their steps run as 'workflow' with the owner's rights (18-workflows.mjs:193), an agent that may change things can save one, and run_workflow clears on any start verb. Every new action (jobs, power, updates, settings) inherits that hole unless it is closed first.
- 'Ask the owner once' is not enforceable today: agents answer ordinary questions themselves (17-changes.mjs:80-87) and a typed 'ok' presses an ordinary button as the owner's click (14-chats.mjs:206-209). Anything that must be the owner's has to be an owner-only question or a check inside the action.
- The passkey rule is by path (22-passkey.mjs:98) and no /actions path is in it; POST /actions also accepts sign-ins made from the internet. 'The owner's own hand' needs a definition in code.
- restore.sh can leave the console stopped and empty (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:134-147), and undo_update, already in the batch in the gate, runs it unattended.
- The safety pause's counters live in memory (16-actions.mjs:268), so any loop that restarts the console never trips it.
- Containers on Spark 2 have two unverified hazards: being vouched for as the owner, and reaching the brain directly on Docker's default network.

Rulings below: 11 unsafe as written (each with the guard that makes it safe), 9 shrink, 3 cut, 5 defer. Build order from a safety view: the saved-workflow and hand-only rules, restore.sh, counters on disk, then update_console; the container fence proven on Spark 3 before anything runs on Spark 2.

Not verified: anything on the live Sparks (Docker's default runtime, how Tailscale's serve labels a local connection, whether the owner's account is Tailscale's operator), and engine flag names.

rulings.proposal: Gap 4: update_console (test and install an update from chat or the API)
rulings.why: This is the proposal that can take the console away. Read in the code: (1) the installer's last step can run `sudo tailscale serve` when a route looks missing, and rewrites the systemd unit at every install (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:334-340, 180-198). (2) restore.sh stops the service, empties the live folders and only then copies, under `set -e` (:134-147), so a failed copy (a full disk) leaves the console stopped and empty. Each snapshot holds its own frozen copy of that script, so a fix does not reach the ten already kept, and undo_update runs it unattended (18-workflows.mjs:362-393). (3) The 12-an-hour and three-failures counts are in memory (16-actions.mjs:268, 07-jobs.mjs:4), so a loop that includes a console restart never trips the pause. (4) The gate container as proposed mounts the source folder writable, so a test can rewrite deploy/install.sh or .git/hooks, which then run on the host as the owner's account (in the docker group, so as root). (5) Plain 'undo' in chat clears undo_update today (16-actions.mjs:160).
rulings.instead: Build it with these guards in code. Install from `git archive` of the commit, never from the folder the tests ran in; mount the tree read-only in the gate with one separate output folder for the lock; run git with hooks off. `self` mode never writes the unit, the watchdog or Tailscale routes and never calls sudo. The updater, probe, watchdog and one current restore.sh live outside the source and are replaced only by an install a person runs over SSH. Fix restore.sh first: copy beside, swap by rename, always start the service on exit. Keep the 3-a-day cap in a file the updater writes. update_console and undo_update get their own intent kind that needs the word update, build or console in the owner's message. Callers: the owner's chat words, or the owner's POST /actions from the tailnet; a sign-in made from the internet gets a passkey question; never the agent door, never a saved-workflow step. It installs only what is already committed in ~/spark-console-src.

rulings.proposal: Gap 8: update_console with a `patch` input
rulings.why: A patch in a request body is code that runs as the owner's account on the hub. POST /actions accepts every owner sign-in, including a long-lived terminal token used from the internet (24-handler.mjs:224-229), and no /actions path is in the passkey rule (22-passkey.mjs:98). The protected-file list cannot make it safe: the parts are joined into one module, so a patch to any part can change sign-in.
rulings.instead: No patch input. An agent pushes a branch into ~/spark-console-src over the owner's SSH (which stays the owner's), and the owner says 'update yourself'. One update_console, the independence area's, with the guards in that ruling.

rulings.proposal: Gap 5, step 2: change_console (Sparkie writes and installs its own code)
rulings.why: Unmeasured (the trial's only run is a dry run with 0 passes), and it is the one path where code nobody read becomes the console. The file list stops honest mistakes only. A test gate can be passed by adding a weak test as easily as by removing a strong one. The trial as built also runs with host networking (agentbar/run.mjs:93), which reaches the editors on 127.0.0.1, a full shell as the owner (21-editor.mjs:2-3).
rulings.instead: Run the trial only after `--network host` is gone. If the action is built later: every install of code Sparkie wrote waits for the owner's passkey button with the changed files listed, and that rule does not relax after a few clean runs. The engine container gets no network, no Docker socket, and a purpose-built socket that passes chat calls to the brain only, never api.sock (which accepts a typed owner login). The task is the owner's words; Sparkie never starts one from its own error log.

rulings.proposal: Gap 2: run_box runs whenever the owner's message is an instruction, with no button
rulings.why: Today's gate checks names (a model, a container, a Spark) against the owner's words. A script's content has nothing to be checked against. In the same turn Sparkie can have read a playbook (20,000 characters of outside text), a log or an earlier try's output, and written it into the script. With the network on, that script can send out whatever it reads and reach the home network and the tailnet from the Spark's own address: other Sparks' model ports, the owner's Mac and phone, the router, later a smart plug's on/off address. The 6-tries-a-day cap is per name, and Sparkie picks the name.
rulings.instead: The fence decides whether content needs a yes. Network off, image from the short list and already on that Spark, CPU only: it runs on the owner's instruction with no button; the worst case is wasted time inside its own folder. Network on, a GPU, or an image not on the list: one yes for that request, kept by code against the image, network and GPU setting; changing any of them asks again. That yes is an owner-only passkey question when an agent asks, or when outside text (a playbook, a page, search results) was read in that request; otherwise a plain button. Tries count per owner request (3 retries inside the request's 12 changes), not per name.

rulings.proposal: Gap 1: workloads, with CPU services and jobs on Spark 2
rulings.why: Spark 2 is the hub, and the proposal leaves these open. (1) Identity: person-level requests are refused only from a list of the Sparks' tailnet addresses and this host's own (23-http.mjs:65-85, 03-identity.mjs:192). A container has another address (172.x). If Tailscale's serve vouches for that local connection as the owner, a container on Spark 2 is the owner on every route. Not checked. (2) The brain runs on Docker's default network with its port published on 127.0.0.1 only (13-main-model.mjs:128-131); containers on that network reach it directly, round the gateway and any owner-first line. (3) `--memory` bounds CPU memory only; if Docker's default runtime on DGX OS is NVIDIA's, an image that sets NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES gets the GPU without `--gpus`, and a freeze there takes the console and the brain together. Not checked. (4) The console writes a spec's `files` into a folder the container also writes; a link left there (to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys or ~/.bashrc) receives the console's next write, made as the owner. (5) `--restart unless-stopped` retries for ever, and nothing bounds disk on the hub; passkey sign-in writes a file on every use (22-passkey.mjs:167-168).
rulings.instead: Keep the design and add, in code with a test each: its own Docker network (never the default, never host); `--runtime runc`, all capabilities dropped, no-new-privileges, a process cap, memory equal to memory-plus-swap, a read-only root with a small tmpfs; ports picked by the console from one fixed range, bound to the tailnet address; spec files in a console-only folder mounted read-only and the data folder mounted apart, with the console never writing into it or following links out of it; only the Hugging Face cache's hub folder and ~/models mounted read-only, never the folder above (the token is there); `--restart on-failure:3`; a disk limit per workload and a free-disk floor on Spark 2. requestGate treats any forwarded address that is private and not a known tailnet device as a Spark's own program. Before the first container on Spark 2, two hand checks from inside a bridge container: /console/api/whoami says access none, and no /dev/nvidia* exists. Prove the runner on Spark 3 first.

rulings.proposal: Gap 3: jobs whose first run 'asks the owner once'
rulings.why: The once-only yes cannot be enforced where it is proposed. An agent that may change things answers an ordinary question itself with the choice id (17-changes.mjs:10-11, 80-87). A saved workflow's steps run as 'workflow', outside Sparkie's gate (18-workflows.mjs:193), so a spec run through a workflow never meets the question. A typed 'ok' presses an ordinary button as the owner's click (14-chats.mjs:206-209). And `set`, or saving again over a verified name, can change the image, command or network after the yes.
rulings.instead: Keep the yes in the spec store and check it inside run_workload for every caller: who approved which hash (image digest, command, files, net, gpu, memory). No record for this hash means a question, whoever calls; from an agent or a workflow step it is owner-only. `set` changes only values the spec declares as settings; anything else is a new hash. A time limit and a disk limit are required fields with defaults. Jobs never mount ~/spark-console-src, the state folder, a socket or the home folder. Output reaches Sparkie as data and can only continue the owner's stored request.

rulings.proposal: Gap 7: run_job and job_result as a second launcher
rulings.why: Three areas propose the same ability three ways (save/run/stop_workload, run_box, run_job). Three launchers are three fences to keep right, and the approval record above needs one stored thing to point at.
rulings.instead: Build one: the use-cases area's saved spec with two kinds. A workflow step names a spec; it never carries a script of its own.

rulings.proposal: Gaps 3 and 4: passing runs save themselves as workflows that never ask; tries excluded from the safety pause
rulings.why: A saved run is a stored script that replays from chat, agents and the API with no question. That is right only when what replays is exactly what was approved. A second copy of the script inside saved-workflows.json can be rewritten by save_workflow, which replaces silently and records the owner as author even for an agent (18-workflows.mjs:164-167). Tries outside the pause, plus a brain turn after every try, is a loop braked only by a per-name counter.
rulings.instead: The spec store is the only home of a script, with its approval hash; a passing run marks it proven there. Retries draw from the request's one budget (8 turns, 12 changes, 2 hours) kept on the task in chats.json, at most 3 tries, then Sparkie says what it tried and stops.

rulings.proposal: Gap 1: ownerCall treats Sparkie in the owner's chat as the owner's own hand
rulings.why: As written it is used at both pause checks (17-changes.mjs:31, 16-actions.mjs:298). Sparkie in the owner's chat would then run through the owner's pause and through the automatic pause that tripped because Sparkie looped. The pause is the only brake on carried-on turns.
rulings.instead: ownerCall is the page or POST /actions, nothing else. Sparkie's turn gets two narrow things: it may cancel another asker's operation when the owner's message asks to cancel, and the first clear request of a message is not counted toward the hourly limit. It never passes a pause. Keep the `x-spark-console` header on /actions (curl can send it) and drop only the Origin requirement.

rulings.proposal: Gap 4, part 4 (and the brain area's drafts): a multi-step request that worked is saved as a workflow by itself
rulings.why: An auto-saved entry is named from the request's own words. The planned name rule (run when the title is in the owner's words) would then match ordinary sentences, and the steps replay outside Sparkie's gate. The learning area skipped this for clutter; the safety reason is stronger.
rulings.instead: After a carried request with two or more changes, offer one button, 'Save these steps as a workflow', with the steps built by code from what ran (the chat-and-API area's version). Nothing is saved, listed in the prompt or runnable by name until the owner names it.

rulings.proposal: Gap 1 (also independence gap 2, brain gap 4, chatapi gap 5): start Sparkie's model when its container is exited or missing
rulings.why: The brain's container has Docker's unless-stopped policy (13-main-model.mjs:128), so Docker itself brings it back after a crash or reboot. A container found exited has almost always been stopped on purpose: by the owner over SSH, or by the console's own switch. The proposals restart it unless /main/stop set a flag, which a hand `docker stop` never sets, so healing would fight the owner on the one model only the owner changes. startMain also stops other GPU users on Spark 2 (brain report), which a heal must never do.
rulings.instead: Start it by itself only when the container is missing, or was left stopped by the console's own operation (a failed switch, which the console records). An exited container nobody in the console stopped becomes an open problem with a 'Restart Sparkie' button in the code-written reply, and stays down. Same preset only, never a stop to make room, twice in 6 hours on the existing record. For agents, restart_sparkie refuses while the brain answers /v1/models and is capped at 3 a day.

rulings.proposal: Gap 5: the watchdog restores the last snapshot after 10 minutes of failed /health
rulings.why: restore.sh as written can leave the console stopped and empty, and here it runs with nobody present. Ten minutes of failed /health has causes a file restore cannot fix (a full disk, a bad state file). 'Newest snapshot under 24 hours old' also matches an install a person just made by hand while debugging.
rulings.instead: Order matters: the restore.sh fix lands first, because undo_update in the batch in the gate already runs it. Then the watchdog may restore once, only in the 30 minutes after a self-update that wrote an 'update in progress' marker (the independence area's version), files only. `--with-state` is never reachable from an action or the watchdog: it would bring back old passkeys, sign-ins and agent keys. Outside that window the watchdog only restarts.

rulings.proposal: Gap 7 (with gap 6's automatic turn): learned fixes tried by plain code for every caller
rulings.why: 'Every caller' includes self-healing and a start triggered by an API call (15-routes.mjs:125). That contradicts gap 2 of the same area (an unattended heal never shrinks the context) and lets one lucky fix cut a model to a 16k context with nobody watching. A record can also be taught by an agent whose input came from the web.
rulings.instead: Learned fixes apply to starts someone asked for (chat, agent, POST /actions). For the watcher and the gateway only sockets-instead-of-RoCE applies; anything else is held with its reason. The cause line is matched as literal text with its characters escaped. The automatic turn after a failed start is offered lookups and try_fix only, and its tries come from the request's budget.

rulings.proposal: Gap 9: at console start, stop the leftovers of an interrupted operation and start again what it had stopped
rulings.why: It adds an actor that stops containers and starts models at every console start, from a replay of events.jsonl. With a watchdog and self-updates, starts become routine, and a console that crash-loops would repeat it each time.
rulings.instead: At start-up, adopt what is running and answering (should-run list, verified run) and report the rest in open problems and in the chat that asked. The settle pass never stops or starts anything; what should run comes back through the existing heal pass and its budgets. Mark each interrupted operation settled on disk before acting on it.

rulings.proposal: Gap 7: smart plugs, power-on, and one unattended power cycle by healing
rulings.why: Cutting power to a machine is the one heal that can damage a disk, and its two signals (a standby-watts threshold, Spark 4 booting when power returns) have not been measured. The healing area skipped this for the same reason. Plugs with a local HTTP API are also reachable by any container that has the network.
rulings.instead: Defer until the plugs exist. Then build power-on only, on the owner's words or a workflow the owner saved and runs. Cut the unattended power cycle from the first version: a frozen Spark is an open problem. Never list a plug for Spark 2. Keep plug addresses out of reach of workload containers (see the missing item on the home network).

rulings.proposal: Gap 6: power_spark turns a Spark off from chat, a saved workflow or the API
rulings.why: It is safe for Spark 2 only through two things outside the action: brainSparks() (17-changes.mjs:384, which is empty if the brain's config can't be read and the local Spark isn't detected) and the owner never adding the sudo rule on Spark 2. 'From a saved workflow but never an agent's key' cannot be enforced today: an agent that may change things can save a workflow with this step and run it, and the steps run with the owner's rights (18-workflows.mjs:160, 193). 'Turn off' is already a stop verb for models.
rulings.instead: The poweroff command is only ever sent over SSH to another host: the code path that runs commands on this machine refuses it, whatever the Spark list says. Its own intent kind needs a power word and a Spark named in the owner's message. Refused while an operation or a download runs there. Not on the agent door; a workflow step only when the owner saved the workflow and the owner runs it. The reply says first that someone has to press the button to turn it on again.

rulings.proposal: Gap 8: read_page {url}, a general page reader for Sparkie
rulings.why: Lookups run with no intent check. A general reader gives a brain that holds the owner's memory, chats and fleet record a way to send them out (a URL with the data in its query, written under the influence of a page or a log). From Spark 2 it can also call addresses inside the house: the brain's port, the editors on 127.0.0.1 (a full shell as the owner, 21-editor.mjs:2-3), other Sparks' model ports, later a smart plug's on/off address.
rulings.instead: It fetches only a URL that is literally in the owner's message, or one on a short host list (huggingface.co, github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com, NVIDIA's docs) that a lookup returned. https and GET only, no redirect off the list, refuse any name that resolves to a private, loopback, link-local or tailnet address, and no query string unless the owner typed it. Build one reader (this or the learning area's find_playbook), not two.

rulings.proposal: Gap 1 (and chatapi gap 3): free-form `flags` and an `image` input on start_model
rulings.why: The check behind `flags` is a deny list (service/dig.mjs:212). That works for recipes a person picks; as an open input it has to be complete for four engines that add flags every release. Flags not on it can fetch files nobody asked for (llama.cpp's model-URL and draft-repo flags, a speculative-config naming another repo; confirm the names with --help in the pinned images) or commit memory outside the measured share, which on shared memory freezes Spark 3 or 4. A recipe's env can also turn offline mode off again: ENV_OK allows HF_HUB_OFFLINE (dig.mjs:246) and the recipe's env wins (05-library.mjs:360).
rulings.instead: Typed fields first: context, atOnce, memoryPercent (never above the measured share), engine. From Sparkie and agents, `flags` come from an allow list of about a dozen named flags per engine (the same list try_fix uses); free-form flags only on the owner's own POST /actions, still through cleanFlags. `image` only from the trusted prefixes, pinned by digest, and a pull is a download the owner asked for by naming it. missing: One rule for what a saved workflow may do. Its steps run as 'workflow' with the owner's rights and skip Sparkie's gate (18-workflows.mjs:193), and only five action names are barred as steps (:132). Needed before any new action: steps run with the rights of whoever started the run (an agent's run is an agent's call, counted and paused like one), and a 'hand only' mark on actions (update, undo of an update, power, resume, settings, restart of the brain) that keeps them off the agent door, out of Sparkie's tools and out of workflow steps unless the owner saved and runs the workflow.

A code definition of 'the owner's own hand'. POST /actions accepts the tailnet identity, a browser sign-in and a terminal token used from the internet alike (24-handler.mjs:224-229), and the passkey rule is by path with no /actions path in it (22-passkey.mjs:98). Hand-only actions should need the tailnet identity or a passkey answer; the code already treats a terminal signed in from the internet as weaker in one place (24-handler.mjs:132).

The safety pause's counters on disk. agentChanges and the failures-in-a-row list are in memory (16-actions.mjs:268, 07-jobs.mjs:4). With a watchdog and self-updates, console restarts become routine, so a loop that crosses a restart never pauses. undo_update is not counted at all: it returns no operation id.

undo_update is in the batch in the gate now with three open edges: any agent that may change things can call it (scope fleet:act, 18-workflows.mjs:402), plain 'undo' in chat clears it, and it runs the restore.sh that can leave the console stopped. Fix these before or with that install.

Overwrite protection for saved workflows and memory. save_workflow replaces an existing name silently and records the owner as author even when an agent saved it (18-workflows.mjs:164-167); the owner's next 'coding mode' would run the new steps with no button. forget_memory lets an agent delete the owner's lines (20-memory.mjs:54-63). Needed: an agent may replace or forget only what it saved itself, the previous copy is kept, and only titles (not agent-written 'when' text) go into Sparkie's prompt.

One memory and disk budget for Spark 2, enforced in one place. Four areas each add containers there on their own (services 6 GB, the gate 8 GB, a coding engine 8 GB, an embedder 4 to 6 GB, the eval's stand-in fleet), beside a brain holding about 80 percent. The 8 GB kept-free rule is not applied on Spark 2 by any code today. Needed: one sum checked against free memory at each start, one heavy thing at a time, and a free-disk floor.

What a container with the network on can reach. From Spark 3 or 4 it leaves with that Spark's tailnet address, so it can call the console's /v1 as the owner without a key, every other Spark's model port, the owner's other tailnet devices and the home network. Closing that is a firewall rule, which is the owner's by hand: one command per Spark (a DOCKER-USER rule dropping the work network's traffic to private and tailnet ranges). The plan should give that command and say that until it is run, a network-on first run needs the passkey. The plan must also settle how a job with no internet reaches the models, which no area resolved.

A lock-out test in the gate. Nothing tests the hard constraint today. A cheap static check: fail the gate if the built server.mjs, worker.py or the self-mode installer contains commands for Tailscale changes (up, down, set, serve, funnel, logout), ufw, iptables, nft, usermod, passwd, sudoers, authorized_keys or sshd. It stops honest mistakes, including Sparkie's own later.

One hand check per Spark that no area listed: whether the owner's account is Tailscale's operator (the installer tries `tailscale serve` without sudo first, deploy/host-on-portal.sh:337). If it is, any code running as the owner, including a self-update, can take Tailscale down without a password. Recommend it stays off on Spark 2.

An 'outside text was read in this request' flag kept by code (set by find_playbook, read_page, search results, guides, a job's output). The earlier two-lanes rule was removed for the owner; two rulings here (first run of a workload, the page reader) need a narrow version of it.

A recovery card that works with the console down, written in the repo and seeded into memory: SSH to Spark 2 on the LAN address, the restore command, how to restart the service and the brain by hand, where passkeys.json is. Plus one drill of it. Every self-update and watchdog proposal assumes this path and none writes it down.

What is installed is unclear, and the tree is ahead of its lock again. docs/reviews-2026-11-11.md lines 85-91 say build c0789b85fa67 is installed with memory seeded; the brief says that batch is not installed. overall:
Verdict. The eight reports are right about what is broken, and most of the fixes are sound. Read together, though, they are 79 gaps, about 25 of them the same change proposed two to four times (the brain keeper four times, typed start settings three times, the container runner three times under three names, save-from-what-ran four times), and more than 20 new actions on top of today's 36. One builder cannot ship that as written, and a 27B model will not choose well among 55 tools.

What Qwen 3.8 27B can be trusted with (from the code, not measured):
- Reliable: filling a typed field with something the owner said (a model, a Spark, a number), because code checks it against the owner's stored words (sparkieCheck and tracesToRequest in /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/16-actions.mjs).
- Unproven: anything it must compose. That covers a request carried over several turns, a container description, a script inside a JSON argument, and a cause line picked from a log. The only evidence is 16 one-message eval cases and one partial run on record (test/eval/).
- Not to be relied on unattended: turning a host-install guide into a container, repairing a failed start by guessing (12 minutes of GLM load per wrong guess), or changing the console's own code (the engine trial has 0 passes on record).
So each compose ability gets code around it and eval cases with a pass bar before the prompt promises it. Code builds saved steps from the audit record, a first run is one button, and a fix is one typed setting offered as a button.

Three facts set the order:
1. Any edit to a function listed in START_CODE (18-workflows.mjs:15-18), or to an action's run, inputs or description, gives start_model and start_model_across a new version. The next real start then validates it. Six areas touch that code separately; it should be two batches.
2. Every build needs the whole gate (30 to 40 minutes on the Mac, per test/README.md). Moving the gate to Spark 2 early makes every later batch cheaper.
3. The brief's state of the tree is out of date. docs/reviews-2026-11-11.md records build c0789b85fa67 as installed with memory, carry-on, POST /actions and seeded memory, and workflows.lock.json names that build. The tree is now one build ahead (I computed 4f371d567af6), and the installer still accepts a stale lock. I did not check the live console.

2. The owner is told, and the API is the owner's hand.

rulings.proposal: Gap 1: workload runner (19-workloads.mjs, spec store, save/run/stop, SearXNG)
rulings.why: This is the right primitive and the only one of the three runner designs to build. But the gate cannot judge a free-form spec: tracesToRequest (16-actions.mjs:180-192) checks only model, container and Spark inputs, and the save pattern (line 113) needs the word workflow. Adding verb patterns for open-ended requests is the fragile part of this code. M is honest only if the 225-line bash stand-in for docker (test/mock/bin/docker) is counted.
rulings.instead: Version 1 is CPU-only containers with two specs the builder writes (SearXNG, script). save_workload changes nothing on the Sparks, so it needs no word check. The first run of any spec that isn't built in is always one button showing image, network, memory and Spark. After a passing check, run_workload is clear only when the whole name is in the owner's words. Put Spark 2 placement behind a setting that is off until the owner says yes, so the build does not wait on that decision. Build it after the two start batches.

rulings.proposal: Gap 3: jobs whose operation ends after 10 seconds, with a second job-result operation
rulings.why: It needs three new mechanisms: a result operation raised by the watcher, a carry-on that knows a job is still running, and a run_workflow wait that does not use waitJob (18-workflows.mjs:197). A long script inside a JSON tool argument is also where a 27B model most often produces broken JSON; today that comes back as a bare parse error from 14-chats.mjs:303.
rulings.instead: Keep the job's operation open until the container exits, with a time limit of at most 2 hours in version 1 and no Spark claimed for a CPU job on Spark 2. Then postResult, carry-on and run_workflow work unchanged. Use the watcher's exit event (19-watcher.mjs:99-105) only for a job whose operation was lost to a console restart. Accept the script as a list of lines, compile it before running, and return the syntax error in plain words. One yes covers that spec's image, network, memory and Spark, plus up to 3 script fixes in the same request.

rulings.proposal: Gap 4 part 2: find_recipes returns catalog.json playbooks as guides with image and ports
rulings.why: The data isn't there. The 29 playbooks in service/catalog.json hold only id, title, description, category, sparks and url. Sparkie has no tool that opens a url, so a guide gives it nothing to build a spec from.
rulings.instead: Leave it out of version 1. Once the runner exists, add the README text from NVIDIA's playbook repository to find_recipes, using the existing webGet and ghFiles in 11-setups.mjs. First measure with three eval cases whether the 27B turns a host-install guide into a working spec. Until that passes, new services are taught by the builder or by the owner's outside agent through save_workload.

rulings.proposal: Gap 4 part 4: Spark Console saves a finished chain as a workflow named from the request (up to 20)
rulings.why: Code cannot name a routine well; it would be a slug of the request's first words. Twenty auto-named entries become a list the 27B must pick from, and the name gate needs names the owner would actually say.
rulings.instead: After a finished multi-step request, add one line: say 'save that as <name>'. save_workflow with from: 'last' builds the steps in code.

rulings.proposal: Gap 2: healing for workloads (watchServices)
rulings.why: On Spark 2, Docker's restart policy already covers a crash and a reboot. The Spark 3 and 4 bring-back only matters for GPU services, which are deferred.
rulings.instead: Build only the rule that restarts a service whose check has failed for 10 minutes, at most twice in 6 hours, and the cut-off-job report. Add the Spark 3 and 4 rows when GPU services exist.

rulings.proposal: Gap 5: answer test for embedding and rerank models
rulings.why: answerTest is in START_CODE (18-workflows.mjs:15-18), so this small change gives start_model and start_model_across a new version. Shipped alone it costs a validation run of its own.
rulings.instead: Ship it in start batch B with the other start changes.

rulings.proposal: Gaps 7 to 10: GPU services, a port per model, the files route, the /svc route

rulings.proposal: Gap 2: run_box and 19-boxes.mjs

Three stores and three name spaces for 'a named thing that runs in a container' is what a 27B handles worst. The spec store is needed anyway for services, which need a stable name to stop, list and heal.

rulings.why: The gate's safety today comes from tying each change to words the owner said. It also needs a stated fallback: the owner's outside agent teaches it once through save_workload or save_workflow, and Sparkie repeats it by name.

One start-path plan. Six areas change code in START_CODE or in the start, stop and restart actions; each such install re-versions the workflows, and the next real GLM start is the test. Nobody planned these as one or two batches with one validation each.

A way to pass long text that avoids JSON escaping. A script inside a tool argument is where a 27B most often breaks. One option: Sparkie writes the script as a fenced block in its reply, and code lifts the last block into the spec (the reply text is already in hand at 14-chats.mjs:294). Whichever way is chosen, the parse error at 14-chats.mjs:303 should come back in plain words.

One memory and disk budget for Spark 2. The gate container (8 GB), the workload budget (6 GB), a coding engine (8 GB; the trial uses 24 GB) and the 8 GB kept free are each sized alone, and nobody has read free memory on Spark 2 with the brain warm. They need one measured budget and a rule that the gate does not run while jobs do. Disk has no guard at all: a job that fills Spark 2's disk stops chats from saving.

The rules in the docs. AGENTS.md says nothing starts a workload on Spark 2, and the contract says healing never stops anything and gives a context floor. Several proposals change these rules. Each batch must change the matching lines in /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/AGENTS.md and /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/docs/contract.md in the same install, or a later reader (Sparkie included) will 'fix' the code back.
